problem: LLM/LVLM-based VLN agents mostly plan over discrete nav-graphs, often by converting vision to text. Prior continuous (VLN-CE) methods rely on depth, maps, odometry or waypoint predictors, and LVLM navigators such as NaVid and Uni-NaVid use extra modular visual pipelines. No prior work post-trains an LVLM with RL for low-level continuous navigation from raw egocentric RGB video.
motivation: The authors want an end-to-end LVLM that maps an instruction plus an egocentric RGB video directly to low-level VLN-CE actions, with no depth, map or odometry. Plain SFT supervises the whole output text but gives no fine-grained, action-level signal for multi-step predictions. Inspired by DeepSeek-R1, they use GRPO-style reinforcement fine-tuning with verifiable rewards to improve action accuracy data-efficiently.
key_idea: Fine-tune Qwen2-VL on egocentric-video/next-6-action samples rendered from Habitat (VLN-Ego) with SFT, then apply GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning with a Time-Decayed Reward that scores each predicted future action against the expert action, weighting near-term actions exponentially more.
insight: (1) The reward is shaped by comparing predictions to expert actions offline, not by closed-loop environment outcomes, so RFT here is essentially sequence-level imitation with a soft, temporally weighted reward. Its shape matters a lot (Table 3d, R2R SR): a hard exact-match reward gives 23.8, below the 24.9 SFT model; uniform per-action gives 25.0, linear weighting 28.3, and exponential decay 30.2. (2) RFT helps smaller models: the 2B model after RFT (SR 25.6) beats the 7B SFT model (24.9) on R2R-CE. More GRPO samples per prompt help monotonically (k=2: 24.7 → k=8: 30.2). (3) RFT enables cheap cross-domain transfer: SFT on R2R only plus RFT on just 10K RxR samples gives 22.7 SR on RxR-CE, versus 22.3 for SFT+RFT on the full 1.8M set. (4) For SFT design, predicting a chunk of 6 future actions beats a single action (24.9 vs 15.1 SR) and 8 actions (22.7). Long-Short Memory sampling has the best SR (24.9) versus uniform (20.8/22.0) and exponential-decay (23.8) frame sampling, though exponential decay has higher OS (34.3 vs 31.7).
method: VLN-Ego data engine: renders egocentric frames step by step in Habitat on MP3D (61 train scenes) along R2R and English RxR trajectories. Each sample holds a system message, instruction, history frames, current frame, 4 action choices, and a GT of the next 6 actions; 630K R2R + 1.2M RxR samples.

Long-Short Memory Sampling: picks history frames densely (interval δ1) within the last M steps and sparsely (interval δ2 > δ1) over older history. Up to 16 images per instance at ≤65,536 pixels each (~4.1K tokens).

Multi-step action text output: the model autoregressively generates n=6 future actions, each as an option letter (A–D) plus a description (e.g. 'B. Turn left 30 degrees'), from FORWARD / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT / STOP.
Stage 1 SFT: cross-entropy on the full action text (option IDs and descriptions) against expert demonstrations. 1.8M samples, lr 5e-6, cosine schedule, global batch 64, 1 epoch (~36 h on 8×A800).
Stage 2 RFT with GRPO: 8 sampled responses per prompt, group-normalized advantages, clipped ratio, KL penalty β=0.04, lr 1e-6. Uses 20K samples (10K R2R + 10K RxR), ~12 h/epoch.
Time-Decayed Reward (TDR): R_nav = Σ_k γ^k · 1[α_{t+k} = α*_{t+k}] over the 6 predicted action IDs, a soft reward that prioritizes earlier actions, replacing the hard 0/1 exact-match reward.

setting.backbone: Qwen2-VL-7B and Qwen2-VL-2B (fine-tuned: SFT then GRPO RFT)
setting.training_data: VLN-Ego (own, Habitat-rendered from 61 MP3D training scenes): 630K R2R + 1.2M RxR-English step samples (1.8M) for SFT; 20K randomly selected samples (10K R2R + 10K RxR) for RFT. Some variants use R2R-only SFT.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB video (history frames + current frame); no depth, map or odometry
setting.action_space: low-level discrete FORWARD / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT / STOP, predicted as a chunk of 6 future actions (turn described as 30 degrees in the example; forward step size not stated)

numbers_note: Ablation tables (Table 3a–d) report only SR/OS on 'R2R Val' with Qwen2-VL-7B trained on R2R only; they are not listed as separate entries. The RFT ablation best rows (30.2/41.2) match the main R2R-CE result. The SFT ablation best row (24.9/31.7) matches Table 1 SFT-7B SR but not its OS (37.1). Embodied QA results are only in the (unavailable) supplementary. The Conclusion/Limitation section is empty in the source. Table 2 also has R2R-only-trained SFT rows (*, e.g. 7B SR 14.9) and a ‡ 2B row (SR 20.7) that are not listed.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, VLN-R1 (Qwen2-VL-7B) using only RGB video reaches SR 30.2 / OS 41.2 / SPL 21.8 / NE 7.0. This beats the listed map+odometry+depth baselines R2R-CMTP (SR 26.4, SPL 22.7, which remains higher on SPL) and AG-CMTP (23.1), and improves on its own SFT stage by +5.3 SR. On RxR-CE val-unseen it gets SR 22.3 (full data) and 22.7 (R2R SFT + only 10K RxR RFT samples), above WS-MGMap (15.0), CM2 (14.4) and A2Nav (16.8). RFT lets the 2B model match or beat the 7B SFT model.
limitations: Stronger contemporary VLN-CE methods (e.g. NaVid, Uni-NaVid, waypoint-based ETPNav-style agents), which report substantially higher R2R-CE SR, are not compared. The comparison set is weak, so the 'state-of-the-art' claim is not well supported, and absolute SR (~30% R2R-CE) remains modest.

The RL reward is computed offline by matching predicted actions to expert actions on logged samples, not from closed-loop environment rollouts or success. RFT is therefore close to reward-weighted imitation and cannot learn recovery beyond expert behavior.

Simulation only (Habitat/MP3D), no real-robot validation. Some reporting inconsistencies (ablation OS vs main table, unclear training data for the R2R table), and the conclusion/limitation section is empty.
